roles.title: C++ Developer - Experienced Hire
roles.eligibility: Experienced Professionals category, tagged 'Immediate Start'. No graduation-year gate. Asks for 'professional experience developing performance-critical applications in modern C++'; no minimum years stated.
roles.requirements: Degree in CS, Engineering or related technical field | Professional experience in modern C++ (C++11/14/17/20) on performance-critical applications | Strong multi-threading, memory management, IPC, STL, Boost, network/socket programming | Deep understanding of performance tuning, profiling and optimisation | Familiarity with high-performance real-time systems; trading experience a plus but not required
roles.notes: Best single fit in the whole SIG in-scope set for this candidate. Team is Trading Technology in Dublin, described internally as 'C++ Strategy Developer'; low-latency HFT systems, works alongside quantitative researchers. Explicitly 'trading experience is beneficial but not required'. EU citizen, no sponsorship needed. Posted 2025-10-01, still live and last updated 2026-07-30, so it is an evergreen/rolling req.

roles.title: Trading Systems Performance Engineer – EMO – Experienced Hire
roles.eligibility: Experienced Professionals. No graduation-year gate, no stated minimum years.
roles.requirements: Excellent software development, testing, troubleshooting and analysis in C/C++ and C# | Extensive knowledge of computer internals, operating systems and networking | Data analysis in Python (Jupyter); Python and PowerShell scripting | Nice to have: low-latency trading environment experience | Nice to have: BGP, IGMP, PIM, Ethernet, IP, UDP, TCP protocols | Nice to have: FPGA, Solarflare, kernel bypass, DC operations

Strong match for the candidate's kernel/GPU performance background, though the stack is network/CPU rather than GPU. Partners with FPGA developers, traders and quant researchers. The equivalent live req is 'C++ Developer - Experienced Hire' (https://careers.sig.com/jobs/9842), an experienced-hire C++ Trading Technology role; a second relevant one is 'Trading Systems Performance Engineer – EMO – Experienced Hire' (https://careers.sig.com/jobs/10810). The row's substance (Dublin, C++ track, EU seat) holds; the title does not.

existing_rows_audit.existing_title: Quantitative Developer — eligibility gate 'New-grad OR entry-level req'
existing_rows_audit.detail: The stated eligibility gate is wrong. The live Dublin C++ req (https://careers.sig.com/jobs/9842) is filed under 'Experienced Professionals' and asks for professional C++ experience — it is not a new-grad req. Conversely SIG's actual Dublin new-grad reqs are the 'Graduate: 2027' trader/researcher programmes, which are gated to a June 2027 cohort start and would exclude the candidate. Also: the row's '€90–140k' figure is unsupported — SIG postings state verbatim 'Susquehanna does not post salary information, so any salary information you find online may not be accurate because it was not provided or verified by Susquehanna.'

Hong Kong office confirmed (https://sig.com/who-we-are/office-locations/), but there is no 'Quantitative Developer' req and no C++ req there. The two live dev reqs are 'Trading Systems Developer - HK' (https://careers.sig.com/jobs/8735) and 'C# Strategy Developer' (https://careers.sig.com/jobs/9209) — both explicitly C#, and the latter demands 5+ years. The row's C++ track label is wrong for Hong Kong, and its 'new-grad/entry-level' gate is wrong too; every remaining HK early-career opening is a Summer 2027 internship. HKD 1.3–1.9M comp figure is unsourced.

Out of scope for this pass (US office). The office itself is real and is SIG's headquarters (Bala Cynwyd, Philadelphia Area) with 103 live reqs, so the office half of the row is sound; the title and the $300–400k figure were not checked and the salary is inconsistent with SIG's stated policy of not publishing salary information.

notes:
Enumeration method: careers.sig.com is an Angular/Radancy front end whose HTML and sitemap render empty to a fetcher, and the /search-jobs/results endpoint returns only the SPA shell. The site's JSON API at https://careers.sig.com/api/jobs?page=N&limit=20 does return structured data; paging through it captured all 241 live reqs firm-wide on 2026-08-04. Canonical public posting URLs are https://careers.sig.com/jobs/<reqId>; the apply links redirect to careers-sig.icims.com. Every role above was read from its full posting text via that API and the URL pattern was confirmed to resolve (HTTP 200, matching <title>).

Firm-wide distribution of the 241 reqs: Bala Cynwyd 103, Dublin 41, Sydney 37, New York 25, Hong Kong 16, London 12, Tokyo 2, Richmond 2, Chicago 2, Shanghai 1. So Dublin is by far SIG's largest in-scope office, and London is a distant second.

In-scope cities with an office but no in-scope openings: Singapore (office confirmed on SIG's own locations page but zero reqs of any kind currently posted), Shanghai (one req, Compliance Officer — out of scope; note SIG also lists a Beijing office), Tokyo (two reqs, 'Investment Principal' and 'Senior Legal Counsel' — neither is a quant/engineering role, so despite a real Tokyo office there is nothing here for this candidate). SIG has no Amsterdam, Paris, Frankfurt, Zurich, Milan or Warsaw office; its only continental-EU presence is Dublin.

ML Performance track: zero matches anywhere in scope. Grepping all in-scope postings for GPU, CUDA, PyTorch, deep learning, kernel and FPGA returns only boilerplate — 'machine learning' appears solely in SIG's standard 'About Susquehanna' blurb, which is appended to nearly every req including legal and recruiting ones. The only genuine hits are req 10810 (FPGA and kernel-bypass, as nice-to-haves on the low-latency perf role) and req 10603 (Linux kernel troubleshooting). SIG does not appear to run an ML-systems or research-engineering function in Europe or APAC.

Roles deliberately excluded as out of scope: Dublin 'Senior Linux Platform Development Engineer' (10603) is Python/OpenStack/Kubernetes platform work, not C++; Dublin 'Quantitative Data Engineer | Options' (9986) is pure Python data engineering asking 4+ years Python and 3+ years Pandas/Polars/PySpark; Dublin 'Software Engineer | Sports Analytics' (9168) and 'C# Full-Stack Developer' (10495) are C#; the three Dublin Site Reliability Engineer reqs are ops/DevOps rather than systems C++; all Summer 2027 internships in Dublin, London and Hong Kong are student-gated and under six months.

Compensation: no figure is given for any role. SIG states verbatim in its postings, 'Susquehanna does not post salary information, so any salary information you find online may not be accurate because it was not provided or verified by Susquehanna.' Every comp_local field is therefore empty, and the existing spreadsheet's three SIG comp estimates should be treated as unsourced.

Bottom line for this candidate: Dublin req 9842 (C++ Developer - Experienced Hire) is the single strongest fit — experienced-hire, EU location needing no sponsorship, modern C++ and performance-tuning requirements that match the llama.cpp kernel work, and no finance background required. Req 10810 is the second. Everything else in scope is either graduation-year gated, C#, fundamental-finance research, or below the candidate's level.
